title: Aurum Alpha vulnerability acceptance
description: An accepted scanner finding (SB2 of standards/085-security-baseline.md): the advisory id, the reason it does not apply or is tolerated, and the date after which the entry is a finding again. The entry lives in each scanner's native exemption file beside the lockfile or Dockerfile; a checker reads the native file and validates each entry against #/$defs/entry, so the native field names are the rendered form and this is the contract. The top level is the checker's normalised view of one such file. The ninety-day window between accepted_on and expires is judged by the checker against the calendar, not by this schema. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this shape; additive evolution per PC6.

source.description: The native file the entries were read from, relative to the repository root (SB2): the lockfile scanner's or the image scanner's exemption file.

acceptances.description: Every accepted advisory in the file. An empty list is a valid file; a missing list is not a file (SB2).

advisoryId.description: An OSV advisory identifier: GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, or a prefix, a year and a serial such as CVE-2025-12345, GO-2024-3105, PYSEC-2024-48, RUSTSEC-2024-0003. Never a package name, a version range or a pattern — an acceptance names one advisory (SB2).

reason.description: Why this advisory does not apply, or is tolerated, in this repository: the defect is unreachable, the vulnerable function is not called, no fixed release exists yet. Required; whether it is true is the review question the ledger row names (SB2).

expires.description: The calendar date after which the entry is a finding again, whether or not the advisory still reports. No acceptance is permanent (SB2).

accepted_on.description: When the decision was made. With it the checker bounds the window to ninety days; without it the checker uses the entry's commit date (SB2).

retire_when.description: The condition under which the entry is removed before it expires: an upstream release, a dependency dropped, a feature removed (SB2).

owner.description: The team or role that made the decision and re-reviews it at expiry, named as a role rather than a person (SB2).

scan.description: Which scan the entry applies to (SB2): lockfile, reachability, or image.
